term-actual-evapotranspiration.s: The part of the potential evapotranspiration that is really taken, limited by the water available in the soil. Abbreviated AET. The soil reservoir computes it.

term-aquifer.s: Rock or sediment saturated with water, which lets the water move and stores it.

term-aquifer-thickness.s: Depth of the modeled layer below the ground surface: 30 m in example 04. This is an assumption. The depth to water table cannot exceed it.

term-attempt.s: One try of a run. A run that failed is tried again in its own folder: the earlier attempt moves under attempts/<n>/, and the run keeps its name and its version.

term-available-water-capacity.s: Water that roots can take from the soil, in mm. Abbreviated AWC. It sets how much water the soil keeps before it lets water pass to the water table.

term-baseflow.s: The part of the river flow that comes from the aquifer. In the model: the water that leaves the aquifer through the drains, summed over the catchment.

term-BD-Topage.s: The reference hydrographic network of France, published by Sandre. HydroModPy can download it as a mapped network. It is not the same product as the BD TOPO.

term-BD-TOPO.s: The topographic database of the French national mapping agency (IGN). Example 04 takes its mapped network from the permanent reaches of this database.

term-calibration.s: Tuning of the model parameters (here K, then Sy) so that its results look like observations. A calibrated result is not, for that reason, validated (see validation).

term-case.s: One point of a plan: a site crossed with a recipe, named <site>-<recipe>. Its run is the folder runs/<site>-<recipe>/.

term-catchment.s: Surface that gathers water toward a single exit point, the outlet. In HydroModPy, it is drawn from the relief and the position of the outlet.

term-cell.s: One square of the computation grid: 75 m wide in example 04. The model computes one value per cell, and the maps count cells. The set of cells that cuts the model area is the mesh.

term-conductance.s: How freely a drain passes water for a given rise of the water table. Unless you declare one, the model derives it from the hydraulic conductivity and from the thickness of the clogging layer of the drain bed.

term-criterion.s: A number that a calibration drives toward a target, over many trials. It must behave well along that search. The same number, only read, is a diagnostic.

term-depth-to-water-table.s: Distance between the ground and the top of the water table, in meters, never negative.

term-diagnostic.s: A number that you read to describe a result, put in a report or use to compare two runs. It is not driven to a target. See criterion.

term-digital-elevation-model.s: Map of the ground elevation, on a regular grid. Abbreviated DEM.

term-downslope-distance.s: Distance a cell travels along the slope before it reaches a network. Written D_{so} from the simulated network to the mapped one, and D_{os} in the opposite direction. It measures how far apart two networks are.

term-drain.s: Condition that lets water leave the aquifer when the water table reaches its elevation, never the reverse. In example 04, the drains are placed at the ground surface and their capacity (the conductance) is deduced from K.

term-ensemble.s: A set of runs of the same model with different parameters or inputs. The spread between the runs shows how much a result depends on those choices. See /understand/how-sure.

term-equifinality.s: Several different sets of parameters reproduce the observations about equally well. The calibration then cannot say which set is right. See /understand/how-sure.

term-excess.s: A cell where the model puts a stream and the map has none. See valid.

term-forcing.s: What drives the model through time: the recharge, or the rainfall and the potential evapotranspiration from which a soil reservoir computes it.

term-gauge.s: The station at the outlet of a site whose discharge the model is compared with. Every observed series and every score reads it, unless a section names another station.

term-groundwater.s: Water that fills the pores of the ground below the water table.

term-Hub-Eau.s: The public interface to French water data. HydroModPy can download the discharge measured at a gauging station from its hydrometry service.

term-hydraulic-conductivity.s: How easily the subsurface lets water pass, written K, in m/s. It cannot be measured at the scale of a catchment: it is calibrated.

term-hydraulic-head.s: Elevation of the water table at a point. It is the unknown that the model computes in each cell; the depth to water table is deduced from it.

term-hydrograph.s: Curve of the flow as a function of time.

term-indicative.s: A reliability label. No field measurement was compared with this result. See reliability label.

term-initial-condition.s: State of the water table at the start of the computation. In example 04, a first month in steady state provides it.

term-interfluve.s: The higher ground between two valleys. The water table is deep under it.

term-intermittent-flow.s: A stream that flows for only part of the year. On the intermittence map: a cell that flows at some time steps of the year, not at all of them.

term-lockfile.s: The file hydromodpy.lock at the root of a project. It pins the fetched data and your own files by checksum, gives the licence of each, and records the version of the code. hmp data lock writes it. Each run also seals the inputs it read in its own inputs.json. See /understand/can-i-check-what-was-run.

term-mapped-network.s: Streams drawn on a map (here, the permanent reaches of the BD TOPO). It is a reference to compare and calibrate against, not an input to the flow computation.

term-mesh.s: The set of cells that cuts the model area. The word grid means the same thing when the cells are squares.

term-missing.s: A cell where the map has a stream and the model puts none. See valid.

term-MODFLOW-6.s: The groundwater flow code of the United States Geological Survey (USGS). It is the solver of example 04. HydroModPy also runs MODFLOW-NWT, an older code of the same family, and a Boussinesq solver written for HydroModPy.

term-NANCON-station.s: The gauge at the outlet of the Nançon catchment. Example 04 compares the discharge measured there with the simulated one.

term-NSE.s: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency: compares simulated and measured flow. 1 is a perfect match, 0 is the same as predicting the mean of the measurements, and a negative value is worse. The “log” variant computes it on the logarithms to give weight to low flows. A run scores it at the gauge over the declared window, and leaves it empty without a window.

term-numerical-check.s: A reliability label. An internal check of the computation, independent of the calibration. See reliability label.

term-objective.s: What a calibration tries to reach: one or several criteria, each computed on an observation such as the stream network or the discharge.

term-outlet.s: Exit point of the catchment, where the flow is measured.

term-percent-bias.s: Volume gap between the simulated flow and the measured flow, as a percentage of the measured volume. Abbreviated PBIAS. It has the sign of the mean error, simulated minus measured: positive when the model overestimates, that is when it is too wet, and negative when it underestimates.

term-perennial-flow.s: A stream that flows all year. On the intermittence map: a cell that flows at every time step of the year.

term-persistence.s: Share of the time steps during which a cell flows, over the whole simulation.

term-plan.s: The list of the cases of a project of many sites, with the resolved configuration of each. A plan is written once under plan/<hash>/ and never rewritten.

term-potential-evapotranspiration.s: Amount of water that the atmosphere could take back from a soil that is well supplied with water. Abbreviated PET.

term-provenance.s: The record of what produced a result: the version of the code, the solver, the input files and their checksums. See /understand/can-i-check-what-was-run.

term-reach.s: A stretch of stream between two points.

term-reanalysis.s: A gridded estimate of past weather or hydrology, made by running a model over all the observations available. SIM2 is one.

term-recharge.s: Water that reaches the water table from the soil. It is supplied, or computed by a soil reservoir.

term-recipe.s: A variant run on every site of a project: a file, or a file with a few keys changed.

term-reliability-label.s: One of three words that tell how far a result can be trusted: numerical check, calibrated and indicative. They are used under every figure of /understand/reading-results.

term-resolution.s: The size of one cell, 75 m in example 04. A feature smaller than the resolution is not drawn.

term-run.s: One execution of a configuration file, kept in its own folder runs/<name>/. Its README.md says its catchment, its period, its version, its checks and its run label.

term-run-label.s: One of four words derived from the checks of a run when it is read: exploratory, calibrated, evaluated or failed. Calibrated means the run comes from a completed calibration and passed its checks; evaluated means it was then scored on a window the calibration did not use. The label is computed on read, so a run sealed by a version with a known defect is downgraded without being rewritten. It is not the reliability label of a figure.

term-runoff.s: Water that reaches the stream without passing through the water table. In example 04, it is given to the model as data and is added to the drainage to form the simulated flow.

term-scoring-window.s: Period over which simulated and measured flow are compared. In example 04, 2001 and 2002; the year 2000 is used as spin-up. The window of a run’s scores is also the default window of a calibration, which may narrow it. Under the network protocol with no window written, the second stage scores from one year after the start of the run. A validation window is taken out of that default: the search never reads its dates, and each trial is scored on them beside its cost.
term-scoring-window.f: In the file: metrics.window, calibration.window, calibration.validation_window, and for the network protocol calibration.protocol.window.

term-seepage.s: Cell where the water table reaches the ground surface and where water leaves the aquifer.

term-seepage-threshold.s: Fraction of the mean basin recharge, over its own area, that a cell must give back to count as seepage: 0.01 % by default. Another threshold changes the network maps.

term-session.s: The record of one calibration, the folder sessions/<name>/: its configuration, every trial and the best one. The best trial becomes a run of the same name.

term-sidecar.s: The small file <file>.json that sits next to a file a provider delivered. It records the variable, the source, the area and period, the checksum, the licence and where the file came from. The sidecars are the data cache: there is no database. A file you provide yourself, under inputs/, is not part of the cache, even if it has a sidecar to state its licence.

term-SIM2.s: Météo-France reanalysis on an 8 km grid, which supplies rainfall and potential evapotranspiration to the soil reservoir.

term-simulated-network.s: Extension downstream, following the slope of the terrain, of the cells where the aquifer gives water back to the surface. It does not result from a hydraulic river computation.

term-site.s: The catchment a file models: a name, and optionally a label, a gauge and a code that identifies it across workspaces.

term-soil-reservoir.s: Simple daily balance: the soil fills with rain, empties by evapotranspiration and lets the surplus pass to the water table.

term-specific-yield.s: Share of the rock volume that drains when the water table falls, written Sy, without dimension. It sets the speed at which the water table empties and refills.

term-spin-up.s: Start of the simulation that is not scored, while the initial state of the model fades out. In example 04, the year 2000. The second stage of the network protocol leaves the first year out when no window is written.
term-spin-up.f: In the file: a scoring window that starts after it.

term-spring.s: A place where groundwater comes out of the ground. A seepage cell is a spring of the model.

term-steady-state.s: Computation where nothing changes with time: the recharge is a constant mean.

term-stream-head.s: The upstream end of a stream, where it starts to flow. The heads dry up first in summer.

term-stress-period.s: Interval over which the forcing is held constant. It is one month in example 04. The solver may cut it into smaller time steps.

term-summary.s: The tables, map, figures and report over all the cases of a project, written under summary/ by hmp campaign collect. It is rebuilt from the runs each time.

term-time-step.s: On the maps and curves of this part of the site, the unit of time of the results: one month in example 04. Strictly, the month is a stress period and the solver may cut it into smaller steps.

term-TOML.s: The plain-text format of the configuration file. One TOML file describes a whole run. The files of example 04 are walked through in /get-started/staircase/index.

term-transient.s: Computation where the recharge and the water table vary from one time step to the next.

term-trial.s: One run of the model with one set of parameter values, tried by a calibration. A calibration runs many trials and keeps the best. The trials of a session are numbered once, across its phases and restarts.

term-uncertainty.s: How far a result could be from the truth. See /understand/how-sure.

term-unconfined-aquifer.s: Aquifer whose top is not trapped under an impermeable layer: it rises and falls freely with the recharge. HydroModPy targets this type of aquifer.

term-valid.s: A cell where the simulated network and the mapped network both pass. With excess and missing, it gives the three classes of the confusion map.

term-validation.s: A comparison of a model with measurements that the calibration has not seen. See /understand/what-validated-means.

term-visible-flow.s: Minimum flow that a cell must carry to count as “flowing” on the persistence maps: 1 L/s by default. It is a convention.

term-water-budget.s: What enters the aquifer (recharge), what leaves it (drainage) and the change in storage. Its closure is a numerical check of the solver.

term-water-table.s: The top of the groundwater: the level below which the ground is saturated. The model computes its elevation in every cell, as the hydraulic head.
